newsitem.title: BULGARIA: World Bank, Bulgaria at odds over grain policy.
newsitem.headline: World Bank, Bulgaria at odds over grain policy.

text.p: A World Bank mission arrived in Bulgaria on Monday to smooth differences over grain trade policy with the government, which has imposed grain export fees contrary to multilaterals' recommendations.

"Our position is to have a grain export tax as a measure to protect local producers and to prevent further increase of the grain deficit and ensuing grain imports," Trade Minister Valetin Vassilev told reporters.
The cabinet is expected to discuss with the World Bank a trade ministry proposal to introduce a 15 percent tax on all grain exports, to fend off further grain import needs.
Preliminary estimates show Bulgaria needs to import more than a million tonnes of grain to cover the gap until next year's crop.

"(Grain) export bans must be eliminated and export tax be lifted. We have no major differences. The only issue is timing and how we get from here to there," World Bank team leader Kenneth Lay told reporters on arrival at Sofia airport.

Bulgaria freed prices and trade rules in line with agreements with the Bank and the International Monetary Fund reached two months ago. But pending grain shortages have prompted the government to seek partial protectionist measures.
"What I am interested in now is to understand where we would be going. I would like to go to our board with as bullish a report as possible about the progress in Bulgaria," said Lay.
The aim of his visit was to ensure that the new reformist government which took office last month will continue the fast pace of structural reform started by the interim cabinet in March.
